SYNTHETIC Debian security-tracker fixture provenance
===================================================

synthetic-debian-tracker-subset.json is independently authored for lindm.
Copyright 2026 lindm contributors. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
SHA256: 43e03fbf230a25f87054e765a136a57826e30b9da215884d3a071ce05e44c47e
No original vendor record, description or vulnerability assertion remains in it.
The prior tracker subset was removed because an explicit dataset grant was unclear.
A software license for the tracker does not establish a license for its data.

Schema references, not copied fixture sources:
https://security-team.debian.org/security_tracker.html
https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/data/json
https://www.debian.org/releases/

Fictional coverage map
----------------------
synthetic-deb-source / CVE-2099-99001:
  bookworm resolved; first fix 3:7.4-2+deb12u3; archive/security versions are newer.
  trixie resolved; first fix 3:8.1-7; archive/security versions are newer.
  forky and sid records exercise ignoring unconfigured suites.
synthetic-deb-source / CVE-2099-99002:
  resolved fixed_version "0" means not affected, not an installed threshold.
synthetic-deb-source / CVE-2099-99003:
  bookworm/trixie open without a fixed boundary; nodsa and postponed annotations
  do not authorize a clean assessment. Future-suite fixed versions do not leak.
synthetic-deb-widget / CVE-2099-99004:
  undetermined remains an unknown assessment without a fabricated fixed version.
synthetic-deb-account / TEMP-0999001-ABCDEF:
  provisional strict-format identifier with a low-severity fix 8.77; no CVE alias.
  The record deliberately has no description and carries a fictional bug number.
synthetic-deb-directory / CVE-2099-99005:
  open with unimportant urgency remains affected, normalized to negligible severity.

All package names, issue identifiers, package versions, descriptions and bug numbers
are fictional. Debian release codenames and field/status/urgency names retain schema
identity. No bullseye entry exists: release 11 must fail rather than imply clean.
The document has no publication/modification/acquisition timestamps or signatures.
Parser-generated tracker URLs reflect schema rules, not real vendor pages for these
fictional issues. The fixture does not prove current vulnerability coverage.

Preserved parser and evaluator assertions
-----------------------------------------
feed/debian_tracker_test.go checks six bookworm assessments; source-only identity;
missing architecture/date; CVE and provisional-ID handling; Debian 12/13 first-fix
selection; dpkg epoch, revision and tilde ordering; exact distro/release/architecture
scope; partial coverage; and raw source digest identity.

Malformed-input cases retain array/null/empty roots, empty/null issues, missing
releases, unsupported statuses, absent/empty/invalid fixes, contradictory open or
undetermined fixes, unknown constraint fields, missing repositories, duplicate
packages/issues, invalid issue IDs, truncation, trailing objects, oversized records,
unsupported/missing suites and a foreign distro.

feed/acquire_test.go retains HTTPS acquisition, expected-byte identity and complete
transport ownership. advisory/vendor_integration_test.go retains source/binary
version divergence, not-affected exclusion, open/undetermined behavior, null dates
and persisted partial coverage. These are controlled database inputs, not native
installations or live vendor matching proof.

The companion synthetic Debian OSV source-only fixture is documented in provenance.txt.
The production tracker endpoint, release mapping and native comparator are unchanged.
Real-feed qualification records remain in lab/ledger.json and the Debian matrix
section of docs/verification.md; repository synthetic data is not that evidence.
